title: Siena nos. 13 and 16: a letter on the Pope and Bologna, deciphered from its plaintext twin

steps.what: Project survey (siena1421): no. 16 identified as the clear text of no. 13; partial alignment (bologna, accordi con). Not taken further; listed as deciphered at the time.
George Lasry transcribed the 553 cipher symbols in CTTS and built an initial key.
Claude Fable 5.1 finalised the key and the transcription from the given plaintext of no. 16.
Whole cipher deciphered; first word (baca?) and 'sabbatte' doubtful.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's decipherment and translation (reading.txt, translation.txt, lasry_report.md) and his key figure key_lasry.jpg with the table key.md; no transcription of no. 13 is in the repository (neither his CTTS transcription nor a project one).

validation.notes: contributed reading: George Lasry's sign-level CTTS transcription and key are not in the repository, so no token alignment can be scored

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the plaintext copy no. 16 (R4804), filed in the same fascicle.
outcome.fraction_read_source: George Lasry's report: 'Solved'; only the first word and 'sabbatte' doubtful

texts.label: No. 13 (R4801), a letter on the Pope and Bologna, [1527-1529] (George Lasry)
texts.summary: To 'V. S. Ill.ma': the Pope's agreements and the delay of his coming to Bologna have left 'qualche ruggine'; the writer would spend everything to abase the neighbours and, claiming some castle, do as Lautrec did when he took Modena and Reggio, 'perché al peggio non si ha sinon a rendere'. Dated 1527-1530 from the content, unverified; no. 16 (R4804) is its clear copy. Decryption and translation are George Lasry's, verbatim from his report; his CTTS transcription is not in the repository.

prior.where: No. 16 (R4804) is the clear text of the letter, filed in the same fascicle; the project noted on 24 Sept that no. 16 is the decipherment of no. 13 but did not rebuild the key.

human: George Lasry transcribed and built the initial key in CTTS; Claude Fable 5.1 finalised key and transcription from no. 16. This project filed his report.
